paragraphs.source_en: ‘What to do?—where to go?’ ‘To see a sick lady who has sent for me.’ ‘What sick lady?—where does she live?’ ‘At Gateshead; in -shire.’ ‘-shire? That is a hundred miles off! Who may she be that sends for people to see her that distance?’ ‘Her name is Reed, sir—Mrs. Reed.’ ‘Reed of Gateshead? There was a Reed of Gateshead, a magistrate.’ ‘It is his widow, sir.’ ‘And what have you to do with her? How do you know her?’ ‘Mr. Reed was my uncle—my mother’s brother.’ ‘The deuce he was! You never told me that before: you always said you had no relations.’ ‘None that would own me, sir. Mr. Reed is dead, and his wife cast me off.’ ‘Why?’ ‘Because I was poor, and burdensome, and she disliked me.’ ‘But Reed left children?—you must have cousins?
